exclusions.name: ons.savings_interest_income
exclusions.reason: Concept, not a weight question: the ONS UKEA HAXV row is households' (S.14) D.41 interest resources in the national accounts (FISIM-adjusted, including the unincorporated-business part of the sector; GBP 95.5bn at 2025) while the model's savings_interest_income is cash interest, so the row is unreachable by design (-82 percent on the v20 national candidate). From 2026-09-22 the fitting anchor for interest is the SPI 2023-24 Table 3.7 interest rows by total-income band, uprated to the calibration year (hmrc.spi.savings_interest_income.*, PolicyEngine/chronicle#280 lane); this row is measured on every evaluation as the D.41 diagnostic and never fitted. Retire only with a declared D.41-to-cash bridge.
exclusions.adjudication: PolicyEngine/microcosm#1006 (issue comment 5812206367, the register rulings María gave in session: ruling R3 of 2026-09-22, the SPI interest rows bound and the ONS row a measured diagnostic; income-anchor lane, PolicyEngine/chronicle#280); previously microcosm#762 A16 (2026-09-03).

exclusions.name: obr.housing_benefit
exclusions.reason: Frame-side gap, not a weight question, decomposed on 2026-09-16 (spine-q design weights unless stated). FRS 2024-25 reports 1.56m Housing Benefit benefit units, 99.9 percent renters, near the DWP GB caseload (1.94m in January 2025 falling to 1.46m by December); the spine carries 1.21m GB reporters (GBP 7.15bn reported) because the SPI support channel re-imputes benefit receipt onto its synthetic households without tenure coherence: 363k of its 449k reporting units sit in owner-occupied households and can never be paid. The engine then pays Housing Benefit only to reporting units with a rented tenure, not drawn into Universal Credit, under the capital limit and carrying the household's rent (rent is the household head's benefit unit's alone; claims_all_entitled_benefits collapses to a scalar, so there is no take-up lever): 407k all-pension-age reporting units were drawn into Universal Credit by the 55 percent take-up draw although they cannot claim it, and the working-age remainder is pared by the means test. On the Q50f candidate the engine pays 235k units and GBP 2.13bn against the OBR GBP 12.10bn (-82 percent); the U8 lever receipt already showed the same lever from the other side (0.85 take-up moved this row from -0.0 to -52.4 percent). This PR gates the draw to units with an adult under State Pension age; the SPI-channel tenure defect is a #840/#145 item; the OBR line also carries supported and temporary accommodation the frame has no concept for. Re-measured on every evaluation with the three Housing Benefit caseload rows; renew or retire on the next spine that carries the SPI repair.

exclusions.name: dwp.jsa_claimants
exclusions.reason: Frame-side gap, not a weight question, decomposed on 2026-09-16. DWP's 71,000 claimants at August 2025 is New Style (contributory) JSA after the August 2025 methodology change that removed inactive claims. FRS 2024-25 reports 63k JSA benefit units at design weights (37k contributory, 23k income-based; 27 records), so the source reproduces the DWP count. The spine carries 178k contributory and 92k income-based reporters (GB, design weights) because the SPI support channel re-imputes benefit receipt onto its synthetic households: 161k of the 181k contributory reporters sit there. The stage-6 legacy_jobseeker_proxy (967k) is consumed by nothing. On the Q50f candidate the row measures 34k against 71,000 (-52 percent) after the solve pares the reporters to fit the OBR JSA spend line. The repair is the SPI channel's benefit-receipt fill (#840/#145), not a JSA rule; the income-based reporters are a legacy-scheme residual DWP no longer counts. Renew or retire on the next spine that carries the SPI repair.

The capped population rests on a handful of source households cloned many times: four of the fourteen bands are empty and 14.2 percent of capped units sit above GBP 1,300 a month against 0.6 percent published, a tail of large families outside London (4.45 children on average, full child elements, housing element near GBP 1,350 a month). The bound total (dwp.benefit_cap.capped_households) and the up-to-GBP-100 band, the one band inside the 25 percent bound, stay in the objective; fitting this band would move weight onto those clones (the #762 zero-band lesson). Measured on every evaluation with tools/diagnose_uk_benefit_cap.py; retire when support exists and the band sits inside the bound.
exclusions.adjudication: microcosm#882 (the 2026-09-16 status comment, issuecomment-5694598278, whose next-steps list this repair works, and the repairs plan María approved on 2026-09-16 with her population ruling on the U8 take-up entry; approver as author per the register convention). Expiry 2026-12-08 aligns the whole UC-repair tranche with the zero-band clock already on the register (microcosm#877), so the next spine re-adjudicates them together. Receipts: experiments/882-uc-repairs-receipts.md (R2 and R5, tools/diagnose_uk_benefit_cap.py on the Q50f candidate and the twins).

exclusions.name: obr.vat
exclusions.reason: Level set by an engine factor, not the weights: policyengine-uk's vat divides household VAT by gov.simulation.microdata_vat_coverage (0.38, a constant since January 2023 with no recorded derivation; policyengine-uk#1996), which folds the household share of VAT receipts (about 70 percent per OBR and the HMRC VAT gap estimates) together with the survey's capture of household spending. The frame's raw household VAT is about 46 percent of the OBR receipts, so the row reads +24.7 percent at design weights and +24.1 percent calibrated on microcosm#1121's head calibration (policyengine-uk 2.122.2), against the 25 percent bound. Fitting it held total consumption 5 percent (GBP 55bn) low on the 2026-09-30 national problem, and a re-solve with the row masked changed no other row's fit (98.5 against 98.4 percent within 10 percent). Measured on every evaluation with tools/diagnose_uk_consumption_taxes.py; rebind when a locked policyengine-uk splits the factor into the published household share and a declared survey capture and the row fits.
exclusions.adjudication: María's ruling of 2026-10-08 on the VAT, road fuel and domestic energy plan (microcosm#1113, microcosm#1123 item 3), decision D3: hold the row out until the engine factor is split. Receipts: experiments/1113-consumption-tax-levels-receipts.md (the masked re-solve of the 2026-09-30 problem and microcosm#1121's head calibration).

exclusions.name: ons.household_electricity_expenditure
exclusions.reason: Published-source residual, not a weight question: the lcfs_consumption stage sets electricity spend from DESNZ Energy Trends FY2024-25 domestic volume at QEP FY2024-25 average prices paid (the level the energy_rake gate checks), and ONS Consumer Trends 04.5.1 sits below it on every aligned basis: CY2025 GBP 26.52bn against GBP 29.60bn for Energy Trends volume times QEP unit and fixed costs (0.90), and 1.11 times unit cost alone; meters against households explains about 2 percent. Fitting the row cut electricity 8.6 percent through the weights (82.9 TWh implied against 93.0 TWh on the 2026-09-30 build), and a re-solve with it masked changed no other row's fit. Measured on every evaluation with tools/diagnose_uk_consumption_taxes.py; retire if the microcosm#1113 reconciliation finds a concept difference to bridge.
exclusions.adjudication: María's ruling of 2026-10-08 on the VAT, road fuel and domestic energy plan (microcosm#1113, microcosm#1123 item 3), decision D1: DESNZ volume at QEP prices stays the level and the ONS rows become diagnostics. Receipts: experiments/1113-consumption-tax-levels-receipts.md.

exclusions.name: ons.household_gas_expenditure
exclusions.reason: Published-source residual, not a weight question: the lcfs_consumption stage sets gas spend from DESNZ Energy Trends FY2024-25 domestic volume at QEP FY2024-25 average prices paid over the published gas-connected share, and ONS Consumer Trends 04.5.2 sits below it on every aligned basis: CY2025 GBP 15.34bn against GBP 18.94bn for Energy Trends volume times QEP unit and fixed costs (0.81), and below unit cost alone (0.955). Fitting the row cut gas 18.9 percent through the weights and the gas-connected share from 84.5 to 78.9 percent against the DESNZ meter share the stage imposes; a re-solve with it masked kept the share at 84.6 percent and changed no other row's fit. Measured on every evaluation with tools/diagnose_uk_consumption_taxes.py; retire if the microcosm#1113 reconciliation finds a concept difference to bridge.
exclusions.adjudication: María's ruling of 2026-10-08 on the VAT, road fuel and domestic energy plan (microcosm#1113, microcosm#1123 item 3), decision D1: DESNZ volume at QEP prices stays the level and the ONS rows become diagnostics. Receipts: experiments/1113-consumption-tax-levels-receipts.md.

exclusions.name: obr.fuel_duties_cars
exclusions.reason: Scope and conversion residual once the stage sets household road fuel: OBR's cars receipts (GBP 14.4bn for FY2024-25, the April 2024 vehicle-type split) include car fuel paid by businesses, and ONS Consumer Trends 07.2.2 for CY2025 at DESNZ 2025 pump prices converts to about GBP 13.5bn of duty, 7 percent below the OBR cars line. With petrol plus diesel levelled to ONS 07.2.2 by the lcfs_consumption stage, the engine's 2025 fuel_duty reads -9.9 percent against the row on its RAC price divisors (-8.1 percent on DESNZ's; policyengine-uk#2169 A), so binding it would pull weight toward fuel buyers to cover business use the household frame does not hold. Before the level step it read -34.5 percent at design weights and -17.7 percent calibrated on microcosm#1121's head, and fitting it raised petrol 21 and diesel 34 percent through the weights; a re-solve of the 2026-09-30 problem with it masked changed no other row's fit. Household road fuel is bound as ons.household_road_fuel_expenditure. Measured on every evaluation with tools/diagnose_uk_consumption_taxes.py; rebind if Microcosm comes to model business use of cars.
exclusions.adjudication: María's approval of 2026-10-08 of the VAT, road fuel and domestic energy plan (microcosm#1113, microcosm#1123 item 3), decision D2, with the binding confirmed on 2026-10-09: the stage sets the household road-fuel level and incidence, and the household-scope ONS 07.2.2 row is bound in place of the OBR cars receipts, which include business fuel. Receipts: experiments/1113-consumption-tax-levels-receipts.md.
